draft.title: Diversification
card: Diversification means spreading money across different investments instead of putting it all in one. It is the idea behind not putting all your eggs in one basket.
If one investment loses value, the others may not. So a single loss does less harm to the whole amount.

Investments that are different from each other protect better. Shares in five companies in the same industry can all fall for the same reason. Shares, property and bonds are less likely to all fall together.
Diversification lowers the harm from one loss. It does not remove risk, and it does not guarantee a profit.
draft.remember: Spread your money so one loss does less harm. Risk is reduced, not removed.

a.q: Why does diversification help an investor?
opts: One investment falling does less harm to the total
It guarantees that every investment will make a profit
It removes all risk from the money that is invested
It makes sure the investor earns the highest return
a.why: With money spread out, a loss on one investment is only part of the total. It does not guarantee profit or remove risk, because some investments can still lose value.
a.clue: Think about what happens to the total when just one basket drops.

b.q: Kai has $10,000 to invest. Which plan is the most diversified?
opts: $3,000 in shares, $3,000 in bonds and $4,000 in property
$10,000 in shares of one mining company
$5,000 in shares of one bank and $5,000 in another bank
$2,500 in each of four mining company shares
b.why: The first plan spreads money across three different types of investment, so a fall in one is less likely to hit them all. The other plans stay in one company or one industry, which can fall for the same reason. Several companies in the same industry is still a narrow spread.
b.clue: Look for investments that are different in type, not just different in name.

a.best: One investment falling does less harm to the total

b.best: $3,000 in shares, $3,000 in bonds and $4,000 in property

problems.detail: The why for (b) says 'The first plan spreads money across three different types', but options are shown in random order. The right option (shares, bonds and property) may not be first, so students could be confused. Name the plan by its content instead.
